package_info.why_malicious: These versions were published via a compromised maintainer account and contain injected code that surreptitiously reroutes users’ crypto transactions to an attacker-controlled wallet, resulting in direct financial theft.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when user initiates wallet connection or transaction via dApp)
execution_context.file_location: dist/umd/index.js (minified main bundle of the package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code injects a rogue WalletConnect modal, intercepts wallet connection attempts, and reroutes transaction data to an attacker-controlled endpoint, resulting in user funds being drained to the attacker's wallet.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code introduces a new WalletConnect flow not present in legitimate versions, intercepts sensitive wallet operations, and exfiltrates transaction data to an external, attacker-controlled domain.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would only facilitate secure wallet connections and never reroute or exfiltrate transaction data. The malicious code hijacks the wallet connection process and redirects funds.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate wallet connectors may interact with WalletConnect APIs, but never with untrusted, hardcoded endpoints or by modifying transaction destinations.
key_indicators: Injection of new WalletConnect modal logic
Network requests to unknown or suspicious domains
Interception and modification of transaction data
No corresponding code or release tags in official Git repository

attack_chain.action: Attacker compromises npm account of former Ledger employee via phishing.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to publish malicious package versions

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes malicious versions (1.1.5, 1.1.6, 1.1.7) of @ledgerhq/connect-kit to npm.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is distributed to dApps and users

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes in dApps, injecting rogue WalletConnect modal and intercepting wallet connections.
User transactions are surreptitiously redirected to attacker-controlled wallet, draining funds.
Ledger releases patched version 1.1.8, removing malicious code and restoring legitimate functionality.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected injection of WalletConnect modals or wallet connection flows
Network requests to untrusted or previously unseen domains during wallet connection
Transaction data being sent to external endpoints not associated with legitimate wallet providers
Discrepancy between npm package versions and Git repository tags/releases
file_indicators: dist/umd/index.js containing obfuscated or minified code with references to unknown domains
Presence of new or altered WalletConnect logic not present in official source
No corresponding source code or tags for published npm versions in Git
network_indicators: Outbound POST requests to domains not associated with official WalletConnect or Ledger infrastructure
Connections to hardcoded, suspicious endpoints during wallet connection or transaction signing
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm package versions that do not have matching tags or releases in the official Git repository. Analyze package bundles for injected or obfuscated code that initiates network requests to untrusted domains, especially during wallet connection flows. Flag any code that intercepts or modifies transaction data and sends it externally. Use runtime monitoring in dApps to detect unexpected modal injections or wallet connection behaviors.
